newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia bourse at record despite political crisis.
newsitem.headline: Latvia bourse at record despite political crisis.

text.p: The Latvian stock exchange on Friday said it had its heaviest trading week ever over the last four days despite the resignation of the country's prime minister, which plunged the Baltic state into political crisis.
"Turnover was more than 1.5 million lats, a high figure, actually an all-time high for the Latvian stock exchange," Armins Kalninsh, trading and settlement director, told reporters.
Total turnover over the four days' trade this week was 1.59 million lats and market capitalisation was 129.76 million lats.
The figures came despite the resignation on Monday of Prime Minister Andris Shkele.
Shkele was seen as a key figure in accelerating Latvia's economic reforms and had managed to get a deficit-free 1997 budget passed by parliament.
But market dealers have said that financial players were confident that reforms would continue whoever was in power as there was general political consensus over the need for reform.
The highest turnover was on Thursday at 580,000 lats.
The most active share this week was Daugavpils Chain maker on the secondary list which turned over 402,963 lats and Riga Transport Fleet on the official list on trade of 325,058 lats.
